title: Contact details — address, map pin, phone and e-mail
body:
In the **Contact** menu item (in the "My page" group) you can adjust where the guest will find you and
how they can reach you: the property's **address**, its **exact location on the map**, its **phone number** and its **e-mail address**.
These appear at the top of the website, in the contact section and in the data provided to Google. If the Map
module is switched on, the map will also show this location.

## The location of the property

1. In the **„Address”** field, type the address the way you would tell it to a guest: town, street, house number, or if
   there is no house number, the land registry number.
2. When you tap the **„Find on the map”** button, the pin jumps to the map based on the address. The status bar then reads:
   **„Placed by the address — check it and drag to the exact spot”**.
3. **Tap the map, or drag the pin** to where the guest stops: to the entrance or the gate. If the house is not
   visible, switch to **„Satellite”** view in the top left corner of the map. On a phone the map can be
   moved with two fingers, while one finger scrolls the page.
4. If you made a mistake, the **„Back to the saved location”** button puts the pin back to where you last saved it.

If the map does not recognise the address (common at a farmstead or with a land registry number), it will display: **„The map doesn't recognise this address — drag the pin to the right spot manually”**. In this case:

1. Type only the **name of the town** into the "Address" field, and tap the **„Find on the map”** button —
   the map jumps to the town.
2. Zoom in on the house (on a phone by spreading two fingers apart, on a computer with the mouse wheel or the **+** button), and
   tap where the guest stops. The pin will move there.
3. **Type the full address back into the "Address" field** (including the land registry number) — otherwise only the
   name of the town would appear on the website. Then save.

## Phone and e-mail

![Screenshot: the Phone and e-mail card on a phone](assets/hu/telefon-email.png)

- You can write the phone number in any format (e.g. "06 30 123 4567"). Right below the field you can see how it appears on the
  website: the line starting with **„On the site it appears as:”** shows the form that will appear on the site (e.g. +36 30 123 4567).
  If you leave it empty, there will be no phone number on the website.
- Both details are **public**. We do not send our notifications here, but to the
  communication e-mail address given on the **Account** tab.

## Saving

Next to the **„Save and refresh”** button you can always see what has not yet been saved: after the word **„Unsaved:”** it
lists the modified fields (for example address, map pin). If everything is saved, it reads: **„No unsaved changes”**. After saving, the **„Saved — your page has been updated.”** confirmation appears, and your website already
shows the new data.

If a field is incorrect (for example the phone number is not a phone number), the error appears in red below the field, and
**nothing is saved** — not even the correct fields. Correct it, and save again.

## On the Map module screen too

At the top of the **Modulok › Térkép, megközelítés** screen there is the same **„Property location”** card, with the same
address and pin. What you change in one place also changes in the other. There, a single save saves the address, the pin and the
approach description together. The phone number and the e-mail can only be edited in the Contact menu item.

The **„Back to previous”** button there only resets the approach fields, **not the address and the pin**.
The pin is put back by the **„Back to the saved location”** button; type the old address back in by hand. An unsaved
pin change is lost when you tap the "Back to previous" button.
